en.title: Diagnosing World Models
en.headline: When a world model learns unevenly.
en.summary: What changes inside a world model while it learns—and which measurements help us understand those changes?
sections: The question behind the project

A world model does several things at once: it interprets observations, forms a state estimate, and anticipates what might happen next. A single score can tell us that something changed without explaining which of these abilities changed.

My interest in this began with CLIMB, where an agent depended on imagined experience. I wanted to understand when that experience could be trusted. At City University of Hong Kong, supervised by Prof. Yangchen Pan, I am studying the measurements that might help answer that question.
One model, different directions

In an exploratory offline study, two internal readouts of the same physical quantity moved in opposite directions as training continued. A readout of the visual representation improved, while a readout of the model's inferred state became worse. The direction repeated in three training runs on the same data split.

The figure below shows selected earlier and later observations, with each run's earlier error set to 100. It is a small piece of evidence for uneven learning within one model. It does not establish where information was lost, or which component caused the difference.
The measurement is part of the problem

A readout is itself a learned model. If it struggles to recover a property, the difficulty may lie in the representation, in the readout, or in the data used to fit it. I have found that changing the readout can change the apparent ordering of internal representations.

That makes measurement checks central to the research. What a readout can recover is one kind of evidence. It does not establish that the world model uses that information, and failure to recover it does not prove the information is absent.
Finding a change, and explaining it

A more detailed diagnostic has to earn its complexity. In the experiments so far, the internal readouts did not provide a consistent earlier warning than quantities already available in the training losses. Their possible value is in distinguishing what changes inside the model.

I am also treating diagnosis and improvement as separate claims. A plausible explanation does not guarantee that the intervention it suggests will work. The explanation needs a test, and the resulting change needs comparison with simple alternatives.
Understanding the present, predicting the future

A model can become better at representing its current observations without becoming better at predicting far ahead. In the current experiments, short-range gains have not established long-horizon gains. Whether the changes improve an agent's behaviour is still an open question.

This is the connection I want to understand: which internal changes matter for the experience an agent imagines, and which measurements can help us reason about that experience.
Where the evidence stands

This is ongoing, unpublished research. The figure is an exploratory observation from three training runs sharing one dataset and split; the evaluation data were excluded from world-model training but have been reused during analysis. It is not fresh independent confirmation or a general result about all world models.

This public note shares observations and research intuition. The diagnostic implementation, specific intervention choices, configurations, and full experimental records remain private while the study develops. I lead the project independently as a Research Assistant at City University of Hong Kong, supervised by Prof. Yangchen Pan, since October 2026.

zh.title: 诊断世界模型
zh.headline: 当一个世界模型学得并不同步。
zh.summary: 世界模型在学习过程中，内部究竟发生了什么变化？哪些测量能帮助我们理解这些变化？
sections: 项目背后的问题

世界模型同时在做几件事：理解观测、形成状态估计，以及预测接下来可能发生什么。一个总分可以告诉我们发生了变化，却未必能解释是哪一种能力发生了变化。

我对这个问题的兴趣始于 CLIMB：智能体依赖想象出来的经验，我想理解这些经验何时可信。现在，我在香港城市大学、Yangchen Pan 教授指导下，研究哪些测量可能帮助回答这个问题。
同一个模型，不同的走向

在一项探索性的离线研究中，对同一个物理量的两种内部读数，随训练呈现出相反的走向。视觉表示上的读数变好，而模型所估计状态上的读数变差。这个方向在使用同一数据划分的三次训练中重复出现。

下图展示选取的早期与后期观测，各次训练的早期误差都设为 100。这为同一模型内部的学习不同步提供了一条局部证据，但不证明信息在哪里丢失，也不证明差异由哪个部件造成。
测量本身，也是问题的一部分

读数器本身也是一个学习模型。如果它难以恢复某个属性，问题可能来自表示、读数器，或者拟合它所用的数据。我发现，更换读数器，可能改变对不同内部表示优劣的判断。

因此，核查测量方式是这项研究的核心。读数器能恢复什么，是一种证据；它不证明世界模型实际使用了这些信息。读不出来，也不证明信息不存在。
发现变化，与解释变化

更细的诊断需要证明额外复杂度的价值。目前的实验中，内部读数并没有比训练损失里已有的量提供一致更早的预警。它们可能的价值，在于区分模型内部发生了什么变化。

我也把诊断与改进当作两个需要分别验证的主张。一个看似合理的解释，不保证它建议的干预就有效。解释需要接受检验，改动的效果也需要与简单方案比较。
理解现在，与预测未来

模型可能更善于表示当前观测，却没有更善于预测更远的未来。在目前的实验里，短期改善尚未带来已确立的长期预测改善。这些变化是否帮助智能体的行为，仍是开放问题。

这也是我想理解的联系：哪些内部变化会影响智能体想象出的经验？哪些测量能帮助我们判断这些经验？
目前的证据到哪里

这是一项仍在进行、尚未发表的研究。配图来自共享同一数据集与划分的三次训练，是探索性观察。评测数据没有参与世界模型训练，但已在分析中重复使用；它不是新的独立确认，也不能推广为所有世界模型的结论。

这篇公开笔记分享现象与研究直觉。研究进行期间，诊断实现、具体干预选择、配置和完整实验记录暂不公开。我自 2026 年 10 月起在香港城市大学担任研究助理，在 Yangchen Pan 教授指导下独立牵头这个项目。

Independent project at City University of Hong Kong, supervised by Prof. Yangchen Pan. Ongoing, unpublished research.

en.title: CLIMB
en.headline: A soft constraint on what an agent imagines.
en.summary: How action feasibility, intrinsic rewards and structured replay help DreamerV3 progress through Craftax-Symbolic.
sections: The project

CLIMB is a four-person research project for UCL’s Open-Endedness and General Intelligence module. I led the project and proposed and implemented its three interventions: a soft action-feasibility mask, episodic spatial and inventory novelty rewards, and novelty–learnability–uniform (NLU) replay.

The goal is to help a world-model agent progress through Craftax’s technology tree. The mask addresses actions whose immediate prerequisites are missing; novelty rewards encourage new experience, and replay changes which experience the agent learns from.
What the mask knows

Craftax has 43 discrete actions. The implementation attaches hand-written prerequisite rules to 37 of them. At each real environment step, an extractor provides a 46-dimensional context: inventory counts, player attributes, nearby workstations, the facing tile, and level-related flags.

For example, PLACE_TABLE requires at least two units of wood and a placeable tile ahead. A rule checks immediate feasibility, not whether the action is strategically useful. Actions without a rule receive no mask bias. This is domain knowledge supplied through privileged simulator state during interaction; it is not a mask learned from pixels alone.
From a failed prerequisite to an action probability

For each action, the rules add up a non-negative deficit d(a,c). A missing quantity contributes max(0, required − available). An unsatisfied Boolean or threshold condition contributes one. If every prerequisite is satisfied, the deficit is zero.

The soft mask subtracts λ × d(a,c) from that action’s policy logit before renormalising the distribution: πmask(a|s) = softmax(ℓ(a) − λd(a,c)). The reported default is λ = 5. This changes action selection; it does not add resources or guarantee success.

For PLACE_TABLE, d = max(0, 2 − wood) + 1[the facing tile is not placeable]. With one wood unit and a placeable tile, d = 1 and the logit penalty is −5. With two wood units, the penalty is zero. A finite penalty suppresses the action while retaining it in the mathematical distribution.
The same rules, two sources of context

During real interaction, the mask reads the context extracted from the actual simulator state. During imagination, that state is unavailable. An auxiliary prediction head estimates the context from the RSSM’s deterministic and stochastic features; the same rules then operate on that estimate.

The head is a two-layer MLP predicting a diagonal Gaussian over the context. It learns by negative log-likelihood on observed context targets, using detached RSSM features. It is trained alongside the world model from the start. Imagination-time masking is enabled after a warmup: 50k environment steps in the report, including 10k prefill. The adjusted distribution is used both to sample imagined actions and in the actor loss.
Why soft rather than hard?

A predicted resource count can fall just below a threshold: wood = 1.95 when an action requires 2. A hard mask applies a very large negative bias to any positive deficit, effectively removing that action. The soft mask gives a deficit of 0.05 and a penalty of only −0.25 at λ = 5.

This lets the agent keep considering a near-feasible action when the world model or context head makes a small error. It is a design motivation; the experiment also tests hard masking directly. In the 1M-step comparison, hard masking performs poorly (MAR 0.019 ± 0.011). Soft masking reaches 0.087 ± 0.004 versus the baseline’s 0.079 ± 0.003; that short-run difference is not statistically decisive with three seeds.

The example below isolates the probability calculation. It uses three equal-logit illustrative actions, not the trained 43-action policy, and is not experimental data.
What changes over longer training?

At 10M environment steps, the course report gives mean achievement rate (MAR) of 0.199 ± 0.005 for the full mask + intrinsic + NLU method, against 0.100 ± 0.006 for the matched 50:50 replay baseline. These are mean ± standard deviation across three seeds, for the final-checkpoint metrics in the report.

The mask-only ablation reaches 0.155 ± 0.008. Intrinsic rewards + NLU without the mask reaches 0.092 ± 0.001. The full method therefore benefits from more than the isolated mask effect in these tested settings. The ablations do not independently identify every interaction between spatial novelty, inventory novelty and replay.

The original report figure below shows achievement rate, distinct achievements unlocked and aggregate forgetting together. The full method has higher aggregate forgetting as well as more progress; this is not a claim of uniform improvement on every metric.
Which achievements become more reliable?

The report’s achievement heatmap shows how individual success rates evolve. It complements the aggregate MAR: the full method reaches and repeats a broader set of crafting and progression achievements than the baseline. The heatmap is descriptive evidence of what was achieved, not proof that one particular mechanism caused each improvement.
What I take from it

Feasibility knowledge can make exploration more productive, while imperfect predictions make absolute constraints risky. The reliance on imagined context is also one reason I became interested in diagnosing world models: when a constraint depends on a model’s internal estimate, we need to understand where that estimate becomes unreliable.

All reported results are from Craftax-Symbolic with three seeds. The feasibility extractor and rule set are environment-specific; transfer to environments without privileged state has not been established. Episodic return contains intrinsic bonuses in shaping-enabled configurations, so the page focuses on achievement metrics. I am project lead and first author of the course report.

zh.title: CLIMB
zh.headline: 给智能体的想象加一道软约束。
zh.summary: 动作可行性、内在奖励与结构化回放，如何帮助 DreamerV3 在 Craftax-Symbolic 中继续探索。
sections: 项目

CLIMB 是 UCL「开放性与通用智能」课程的四人研究项目。我牵头项目，并提出和实现了三项干预：动作可行性软掩码、基于空间与物品状态的回合内新颖性奖励，以及新颖性–可学习性–均匀（NLU）回放。

目标是帮助世界模型智能体沿 Craftax 的科技树前进。Mask 处理缺少即时前提条件的动作；新颖性奖励鼓励新经验；回放则改变智能体从哪些经验中学习。
Mask 知道什么？

Craftax 有 43 个离散动作，实现为其中 37 个动作写了前提规则。真实环境每一步都从游戏状态提取一个 46 维上下文，包括物品数量、玩家属性、附近工作台、面向的格子，以及关卡相关标志。

例如 PLACE_TABLE 需要至少两份木头，且面前的格子允许放置。规则检查的是动作当前能否执行，不是它在策略上是否有用。没有规则的动作不添加 mask 偏置。这使用了来自模拟器状态的特权信息和领域知识，并不是单靠像素学出的 mask。
前提不满足，如何改变动作概率？

规则为每个动作累加非负缺口 d(a,c)。缺少数量时，贡献 max(0, 所需数量 − 当前数量)；布尔条件或阈值条件不满足时，贡献 1。所有前提都满足，缺口就是零。

软掩码在动作的策略 logit 上减去 λ × d(a,c)，再重新归一化概率：πmask(a|s) = softmax(ℓ(a) − λd(a,c))。报告默认 λ = 5。这改变的是动作选择，不会补足资源，也不保证动作成功。

PLACE_TABLE 的缺口为 d = max(0, 2 − 木头数量) + 1[面前格子不可放置]。木头为 1、格子可放置时，d = 1，logit 惩罚为 −5；木头为 2 时惩罚为零。有限惩罚抑制动作，但在数学概率分布中仍保留它。
同一套规则，两种上下文来源

真实交互时，mask 使用实际模拟器状态提取的上下文。想象过程中没有真实游戏状态，因此用辅助预测头，从 RSSM 的确定性与随机性特征估计上下文，再把同一套规则应用到估计值上。

预测头是两层 MLP，为上下文预测对角高斯分布。训练目标是观测上下文的负对数似然，输入的 RSSM 特征使用停止梯度。它从开始就与世界模型同时训练。想象中的 mask 在 warmup 后启用：报告中为 50k 环境步，包含 10k prefill。调整后的分布既用于采样想象动作，也用于 actor 损失。
为什么用 soft，而不是 hard？

预测的资源数量可能略低于门槛，例如动作需要 2 份木头，模型却预测为 1.95。Hard mask 对任何正缺口施加极大的负偏置，近似移除动作；soft mask 的缺口只有 0.05，在 λ = 5 时惩罚仅为 −0.25。

这样，当世界模型或上下文预测头有小误差时，智能体仍能考虑一个接近可行的动作。这是设计动机，实验也直接比较了 hard mask。在 1M 步对比中，hard mask 表现很差（MAR 0.019 ± 0.011）；soft mask 为 0.087 ± 0.004，基线为 0.079 ± 0.003。三个种子下，这个短程差异尚不足以作显著结论。

下方示例只展示概率计算，使用三个初始 logit 相同的示意动作，不是训练出的 43 动作策略，也不是实验数据。
训练更久之后，发生了什么？

10M 环境步时，课程报告中完整的 mask + 内在奖励 + NLU 方法，其平均成就达成率（MAR）为 0.199 ± 0.005，同预算 50:50 回放基线为 0.100 ± 0.006。数值为三个种子的均值 ± 标准差，采用报告中的最终 checkpoint 指标。

只用 mask 的消融为 0.155 ± 0.008；不使用 mask、只用内在奖励 + NLU 为 0.092 ± 0.001。因此在所测设置下，完整方法的收益超过单独 mask 的效果。这些消融没有分别识别空间新颖性、物品新颖性与回放之间的所有交互。

下方报告原图同时展示成就达成率、解锁的不同成就数量与总体遗忘。完整方法在取得更多进展的同时，总体遗忘也更高；不能声称所有指标都改善。
哪些成就变得更稳定？
报告的成就热图展示各个成就的成功率如何变化。它补充了总量 MAR：相比基线，完整方法能触及并反复完成更多合成与进阶成就。热图描述达成了什么，并不单独证明每项改善由哪一种机制引起。
我从中学到什么？

可行性知识可能让探索更有效，而预测的不完美让绝对约束带来风险。对想象上下文的依赖，也是我后来研究世界模型诊断的动机之一：当约束取决于模型的内部估计时，我们需要理解这个估计在哪里不再可靠。

所有报告结果都来自 Craftax-Symbolic、三个种子。可行性提取器和规则针对该环境设计，尚未验证在没有特权状态的环境中的迁移。加入内在奖励的配置，其回合 return 包含奖励塑形，因此本页主要使用成就指标。我是项目负责人及课程报告第一作者。

en: Hand-written rules turn a context vector into per-action deficits. The soft mask subtracts λ × deficit from policy logits. Real interaction uses simulator context; imagination uses a learned RSSM context head.
A slightly wrong imagined resource count can make a hard mask remove a valid action. A graded logit penalty leaves room for prediction error. The full page includes an interactive example.
At 10M steps, MAR is 0.199 ± 0.005 for the full method, 0.155 ± 0.008 for mask only, and 0.100 ± 0.006 for the matched baseline (three seeds). Original report figures are on the full page.

想象中的资源数量稍有偏差，hard mask 就可能移除本来可行的动作。分级的 logit 惩罚给预测误差留出空间，完整页面包含交互示例。
10M 步时，完整方法 MAR 为 0.199 ± 0.005，只用 mask 为 0.155 ± 0.008，同预算基线为 0.100 ± 0.006（三个种子）。报告原图见完整页面。

en.title: OpenQFT
en.headline: Learning to discover. Learning from discovery.
en.summary: Some thoughts on scientific discovery, useful experience, and what it means for an agent to keep learning.
sections: What should an agent learn from discovery?

I keep coming back to two questions. Can an agent work out something unfamiliar by choosing its own experiments? And when it encounters a new problem, does the earlier investigation make it a better learner?

OpenQFT grew out of wanting to study these questions together. A successful investigation is interesting in its own right. I am even more interested in what survives it: a useful idea, a better question, or a habit of checking an explanation before trusting it.
An intuition from the history of science

One inspiration is the history of particle physics. Observations arrived before a complete explanation. Researchers had to look for regularities, ask what those regularities implied, and decide which observation might change the picture. An explanation earned its value by helping them anticipate something they had not yet seen.

What interests me is this movement between evidence and explanation. Each discovery changes the questions that become worth asking. Experience can do more than supply another answer; it can change how the next investigation begins.
A snapshot across models

The snapshot now covers five models: GPT-6 Luna (gpt-6-luna), DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (deepseek-flash), GPT-6.1 Terra (gpt-6.1-terra), GPT-6.2 Sol (gpt-6.2-sol) and Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5). All scores are expressed as a percentage of the theoretical maximum: a perfect score is 100%.

The initial evaluation is twice as large as in the earlier version of this note, and every model was evaluated on the same set, so these numbers replace the earlier ones. Complete and Partial describe study coverage, not task success. The experience study is complete for the first four models. Claude Opus 5.5 has initial-evaluation results only.

The table separates initial evaluation from the experience comparison. They use different evaluation subsets, so a change between these columns should not be read as an improvement over time. The averages also hide how much single investigations by one model differ. Claude Opus 5.5 has the highest average here, yet its lead over GPT-6.2 Sol is within that spread, and its own investigations fall into two groups: some reach much of the explanation and some reach little. These are descriptive snapshots, rather than a definitive ranking.
Collecting evidence is only part of the work

Choosing an experiment and making sense of its outcome are different abilities. An agent can collect observations while still missing a useful explanation. It can also settle on a plausible story too early and keep gathering evidence that fits it.

The comparison below places each model alongside a diagnostic reference analysis that works from that model's own observations. The reference also receives additional information, so the gap does not isolate a reasoning deficit. Still, the pattern is the same for all five models: the observations a model collected would have supported much more than the model concluded from them. It is a prompt to ask which parts of an investigation need help, rather than a claim that every answer was already available to the agent.
Models investigate in different ways

The models also differ in how they work, apart from how well they score. One difference is when the thinking happens. GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.1 Terra tend to run their experiments in a few large batches and do most of their analysis after the last one, when nothing they work out can change what they try. Claude Opus 5.5 alternates: more than half of its analysis happens while it can still choose another experiment, and it varies the conditions of its experiments more widely.

The figure shows this as the share of analysis steps taken before the last experiment. A higher share is not a score: GPT-6 Luna and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash also analyse between experiments and score lowest, so alternating does not make an investigation succeed by itself. What I take from it is that the way an agent investigates can be measured alongside its result, and that an explanation worked out after the last experiment can no longer be tested by one.
When experience helps—and when it gets in the way

A later investigation need not begin from an empty page. In the comparison below, each model meets the same problems without and with notes from its own earlier investigations. The benefit grows with what a model can discover in the first place: GPT-6 Luna, which discovers little, gains little, and GPT-6.2 Sol gains the most.

What experience changes differs from model to model. With its notes, GPT-6.2 Sol runs different experiments: fewer of them, with the conditions varied more widely. GPT-6.1 Terra runs much the same experiments as before and changes what it concludes from them. In the cases I have so far, the notes also help with kinds of rule that the earlier investigations had not contained, which suggests that what carries over is mostly a way of working, more than a list of facts.

But useful memory needs judgement. A good explanation can guide a new experiment; an untested assumption can guide it in the wrong direction, and I see both. I want to understand how an agent can carry forward what it has learnt while staying willing to revise it. Claude Opus 5.5 has no experience comparison to show yet. These descriptive means do not imply that memory helps every investigation.
The question I want to keep asking

For me, the exciting possibility is an agent whose experience improves the way it investigates. It notices when an explanation stops working, asks a more revealing question, and brings a useful idea to an unfamiliar problem.

That connects scientific discovery to continual learning: progress in one investigation becomes part of how the next one is approached. OpenQFT is where I am exploring that connection.
A research note, while the work develops

This is an intuition-led preview of independent, unpublished research. Figures show selected descriptive means, with 100% marking the theoretical maximum for the measure in each figure. The diagnostic measure, the process measure and the overall evaluation score are different measures, and the process measure is not a score. Study coverage is marked explicitly. Experimental mechanisms and the full paper remain private while the work develops.

zh.title: OpenQFT
zh.headline: 学会发现，也从发现中学习。
zh.summary: 关于科学发现、有用的经验，以及智能体如何持续学习的一些思考。
sections: 智能体应该从发现中学到什么？

我一直在想两个问题：智能体能否通过自己选择的实验，理解一个陌生的系统？当它遇到新问题时，之前的探索会不会让它更善于学习？

OpenQFT 源于把这两个问题放在一起研究的想法。完成一次探索本身很有意思，但我更关心探索之后留下了什么：一个有用的想法、一个更好的问题，或者在相信解释之前先检验它的习惯。
来自科学史的直觉

一个灵感来自粒子物理的发展史。观测往往先于完整的解释出现。研究者需要从中寻找规律，追问规律意味着什么，再决定什么样的新观测可能改变现有认识。一个解释的价值，体现在它能否帮助预见尚未观察到的东西。

我感兴趣的是证据与解释之间的往返。每一次发现，都会改变接下来值得追问的问题。经验除了提供另一个答案，也可能改变下一次探索的起点。
几种模型的结果快照

结果快照现在包括五个模型：GPT-6 Luna（gpt-6-luna）、DeepSeek V4.1 Flash（deepseek-flash）、GPT-6.1 Terra（gpt-6.1-terra）、GPT-6.2 Sol（gpt-6.2-sol）和 Claude Opus 5.5（claude-opus-5-5）。分数均按理论满分换算为百分比：满分为 100%。

初始评测的规模是这篇笔记上一版的两倍，而且所有模型都在同一组评测上完成，因此这里的数字取代之前的数字。Complete 和 Partial 表示研究的完成状态，不表示任务成功率。前四个模型的经验研究已经完整；Claude Opus 5.5 目前只有初始评测结果。

表格将初始评测与经验对比分开。两者使用不同的评测子集，因此不能将跨列差值理解为随时间提升。均值还掩盖了一点：同一个模型的各次探索之间差别很大。Claude Opus 5.5 在这里的均值最高，但它对 GPT-6.2 Sol 的领先幅度并未超出这种波动；它自己的探索也分成两类，有些得到了解释的大部分，有些所得甚少。这些是描述性的结果快照，不作为最终排名。
收集证据，只是工作的一部分

选择实验和理解结果，是两种不同的能力。智能体可能积累了许多观测，却仍然错过一个有用的解释；也可能过早相信一个看似合理的故事，此后只收集符合它的证据。

下图把每个模型与一个诊断性的参考分析放在一起，参考分析使用的正是该模型自己收集到的观测。参考分析还获得了额外信息，因此差距不能单独归因于推理能力。不过五个模型呈现出同样的情况：模型收集到的观测，本可以支持比它实际得出的多得多的结论。它促使我追问探索中的哪些环节需要帮助，而不是断言答案早已完整地呈现在智能体面前。
模型的探索方式各不相同

除了分数高低，模型的工作方式也不一样。一个差别在于思考发生在什么时候。GPT-6.2 Sol 和 GPT-6.1 Terra 倾向于把实验分成几大批做完，大部分分析都放在最后一次实验之后，这时无论想明白什么，都已经无法改变要做的实验。Claude Opus 5.5 则是交替进行：它一半以上的分析发生在还能再选一个实验的时候，实验条件也变化得更多。

下图用“最后一次实验之前完成的分析步骤占比”来表示这一点。占比高并不等于分数高：GPT-6 Luna 和 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 同样会在实验之间做分析，分数却最低，可见光靠交替并不能让探索成功。我从中看到的是：智能体的探索方式可以和结果一起被测量；而在最后一次实验之后才想出的解释，已经没有实验可以检验它了。
经验何时有用，又何时会妨碍探索？

后一次探索不必从空白开始。在下方的对比中，每个模型分别在没有和带有自己先前探索笔记的情况下，面对同样的问题。模型本身能发现的越多，经验带来的收益越大：GPT-6 Luna 发现得很少，收益也很小；GPT-6.2 Sol 的收益最大。

经验改变了什么，也因模型而异。带着笔记的 GPT-6.2 Sol 会做不一样的实验：次数更少，条件变化更多。GPT-6.1 Terra 做的实验和之前差不多，改变的是它从实验中得出的结论。在目前已有的例子里，笔记对先前探索中没有出现过的规律类型同样有帮助，这说明延续下来的主要是一种工作方法，而不只是一份事实清单。

但如何使用记忆，同样需要判断。好的解释可以指引下一次实验，未经检验的假设也可能把探索带偏，这两种情况我都看到了。我想理解的是：智能体如何带着已有知识继续前进，同时保留修订它的意愿。Claude Opus 5.5 暂无经验对比。这些描述性均值并不意味着记忆会帮助每一次探索。
我想继续追问的问题

让我期待的，是一个能让经验改善自身探索方式的智能体。它能注意到解释何时不再适用，提出更有启发性的问题，也能把一个有用的想法带到陌生的问题中。

这把科学发现与持续学习联系起来：一次探索中的进展，成为下一次探索方式的一部分。OpenQFT 是我探索这条联系的研究项目。
写在研究进行中
这是尚未发表的独立研究的一篇直觉笔记。图中展示选取结果的描述性均值，100% 表示每张图中相应指标的理论满分。诊断指标、过程指标与整体评测分数是不同的指标，其中过程指标不是分数。研究完成状态已分别标注。研究进行期间，具体实验机制与论文全文仍暂不公开。

en: Can an agent learn to investigate an unfamiliar system, and use that experience to approach the next problem better?

en.title: Temporal Routing
sections: MSc dissertation

Encoder-Based Temporal Routing for Software Engineering Agents: An Empirical Study of Trajectory-Conditioned Value Estimation. Dissertation supervisor: Professor Ilija Bogunovic (UCL). Thesis mark: 77.5/100.
The model

A roughly 149M-parameter ModernBERT trajectory encoder with task-conditioned pooling and causal temporal modelling. The work examines whether partial agent trajectories contain useful information for cost-aware decisions.
What the audits establish

Preregistered multi-seed, bootstrap, fixed-budget, and cross-domain audits exposed sensitivity to model pair, domain, and model selection. The dissertation does not establish a universally deployable routing policy.
Follow-up research

Current empirical work separates aggregate prediction of task difficulty from discrimination among attempts at the same task. Early prefixes can mostly rank tasks; within-task discrimination appears later, with limited selection and pruning benefits in the evaluated settings. This follow-up remains a manuscript in development.

zh.title: 时序路由与轨迹预测
sections: 硕士论文
Encoder-Based Temporal Routing for Software Engineering Agents: An Empirical Study of Trajectory-Conditioned Value Estimation。UCL 硕士论文，硕士论文导师为 Professor Ilija Bogunovic。 硕士论文成绩：77.5/100。
模型
采用约 149M 参数的 ModernBERT 编码智能体轨迹，并结合任务条件池化与因果时序建模，研究部分执行轨迹能否为成本敏感决策提供有用信息。
审计结论
预注册、多种子、bootstrap、固定预算与跨域审计发现，结果受到模型对、任务域与模型选择的影响。论文没有建立普适、可部署的路由策略。
后续研究
当前实证工作区分总体题目难度预测与同题不同尝试的判别。早期前缀可能主要对题目排序；题内判别在后期出现，并在已评估设置下带来有限的选择与剪枝收益。这部分仍是开发中的研究手稿。

en.title: SWE-Router
sections: The question
When should a multi-turn coding agent switch models? This collaborative project studies cost-aware routing from partial execution trajectories.
My contribution
I ran official SWE-bench and SWE-Smith grading in containers, collected multi-model trajectories with per-step cost annotations, and contributed to the public Hugging Face datasets.
A research thought
Intermediate behaviour becomes useful evidence when it is connected to a verifiable outcome. Collection, isolation, grading, and reproduction are central to that connection.
Research output
Co-authored work presented at the ICML 2026 Deep Learning for Code Workshop. The linked paper describes the collaborative method and findings.

zh.title: SWE-Router
sections: 研究问题
多轮编程智能体何时应该切换模型？这项合作研究从部分执行轨迹出发，研究成本敏感的模型路由。
我的贡献
我在容器中运行 SWE-bench 和 SWE-Smith 官方评测，采集带逐步成本标注的多模型轨迹，并参与公开的 Hugging Face 数据集工作。
研究思考
智能体的中间行为需要连接到可验证的结果，才能成为有用的证据。采集、隔离、评分与复现是这条连接的核心。
研究产出
共同作者论文，发表于 ICML 2026 Deep Learning for Code Workshop。完整合作方法与结果见所附论文。

en.title: RopeBand
sections: The question
Can rotations that respect RoPE geometry help dynamic 4-bit quantisation? The project connects a mathematical characterisation with an empirical test.
Theory
The work characterises rotations that commute with RoPE and derives closed-form optimal angles for a scoped variance surrogate.
What the experiments show

The evaluated pairwise-only transforms did not outperform full-head Hadamard. The study examines the mismatch between the surrogate objective, mixing support, and the scale statistic used by the quantiser.
A research thought
An optimum for a surrogate is a precise mathematical statement. Whether that optimum improves the deployed computation is a separate question, which the experiments must answer.
Status
First author; under review at TMLR. The preprint is linked below.

zh.title: RopeBand
sections: 研究问题
尊重 RoPE 几何结构的旋转，能否帮助动态 4-bit 量化？项目将数学刻画与实证检验连接起来。
理论
工作刻画与 RoPE 可交换的旋转族，并为限定的方差代理目标推导闭式最优角。
实验发现
所测逐对旋转未优于全头 Hadamard。研究分析代理目标、混合支持与量化器定标统计量之间的失配。
研究思考
代理目标上的最优解是一个精确的数学结论。它是否改善实际计算，需要由另一个实证问题来回答。
状态
第一作者，TMLR 审稿中。预印本链接见下方。

en.title: RentCompass
sections: The product
An independently built UK rental agent for listing searches, commute planning, and neighbourhood comparison.
What I built
Structured conversational state, a bounded function-calling loop, evidence checks, optional MCP tools, and recoverable multi-turn sessions. Releases support rollback.
A design thought
A housing decision depends on several constraints at once. Keeping those constraints in structured state allows the conversation to connect tool-backed evidence to the next practical decision.
Current status
Deployed product. Visit the live site through the link below.

zh.title: RentCompass
sections: 产品
独立构建的英国租房智能体，支持房源搜索、通勤规划和社区比较。
实现内容
结构化会话状态、有界函数调用循环、证据核查、可选 MCP 工具，以及可恢复的多轮会话。发布流程支持回滚。
设计思考
租房决策同时依赖多个约束。将约束保存在结构化状态中，才能让对话把工具提供的证据连接到下一步实际决策。
当前状态
已部署产品，可通过下方链接访问。
